newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Caracas stocks close off as locals take profits.
newsitem.headline: Caracas stocks close off as locals take profits.

text.p: Caracas stocks closed off for the second consecutive session on local investor profit-taking, traders said.
But foreign buyers maintained their positions and the bolsa's long term trend remains up, traders added.
"The adjustment was expected after so many days of outrageous rises," Amerival broker Juan Domingo Perez said.
"But foreign funds did not appear to be closing their positions, although they have slowed buying ... they're waiting to come in on a steeper dip," he added.

The market's 19-share .IBC index slipped 1.1 percent to end at 9,259.33 points as turnover slowed to 45 million shares worth 9.4 billion bolivars ($19 million), according to preliminary figures from the exchange.
"The foreign buying continues, but not as aggressively as in recent days," said Bancaracas broker Ricardo Larrazabal.
Among traded stocks, 23 fell, 20 rose and five closed flat. Merinvest's composite .MRCP index, which includes telephone company CANTV, meanwhile lost 0.9 percent to close at 145.24 points.
